title.en: The role of government and taxes

text.en: The road to your school, the police station, the ration shop: someone has to pay for them. Governments collect taxes and spend them on services for everyone. This lesson explains what governments do and how taxes work.

The government's roles include defence, foreign policy, conduct of periodic elections, law and order, and public administration and provision of public goods.
Local governments provide civic facilities like local roads, drainage, drinking water and waste collection and disposal.
Governments also redistribute income and reduce poverty by taxing higher incomes more and giving the very poor food, shelter, education, healthcare and income support.
Tax is levied by the government for the development of the state's economy; the word comes from taxation, which means an estimate.
Direct taxes are levied on the income of persons, while indirect taxes are levied on goods and services.
The revenue of the government depends on direct and indirect taxes, which are its financial sources.
The Union government has a judicial system to settle disputes, and the state governments administer the police.

problem.en: Why do high-income people pay more tax than the poor, and where does the money go?

text.en: A tax system that takes more from the rich can fund help for the poor.
The money funds defence, roads, schools and hospitals.
Direct taxes fall on income; indirect taxes are paid when we buy goods.

prompt.en: Differentiate between direct and indirect taxes with an example of each.

requiredIdeas.en: Direct tax on income, for example income tax
Indirect tax on goods and services, for example GST

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking only rich people pay indirect taxes

points.en: Governments provide defence, law and order, public goods and local services.
Direct tax is on income; indirect tax is on goods and services.
Taxes also help to reduce poverty and inequality.
